_meta.note: Feature: `hb viz --serve` — a LIVE DAG dashboard for the plugin (node) runtime. Today hb-viz.js renders SERVER-SIDE once and bakes dag.json+state.json into a self-contained dag-view.html; to see current execution state you must regenerate the file. The reason it's baked (not read live from the browser) is that a file://-opened page cannot fetch() sibling JSON — browsers block local fetch. So 'read the data directly and stay current' REQUIRES something serving over HTTP. This adds that: a tiny loopback-only node http server whose GET /state re-reads dag.json+state.json FRESH on every request and returns the SAME server-rendered fragment (one renderer, no client-side render fork). Snapshot mode stays byte-identical (T14 unchanged). Security mirrors py serve_http: loopback bind only, Origin header validated (DNS-rebinding), non-loopback bind refused without --allow-remote. viz is node-only (no python viz today) and NOT a parity surface, so no python mirror is required. Spec-first: the proof reproduces the need (fails on current code, which has no --serve) before the implementation lands.

phases.title: Live DAG dashboard: hb viz --serve (node runtime)

tasks.title: Author the behavioral proof (spec-first)
tasks.description:
Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/viz-serve.sh — a deterministic proof that MUST fail on the current code (no --serve flag exists yet) and pass only once the feature lands. Start with `set -euo pipefail`; every sub-check exits non-zero on failure (a skipped/errored check can NOT yield the marker). Derive the repo root from the script's own path; bootstrap ONE throwaway project into a temp dir via `HB_NO_GIT=1 bash plugin/bootstrap.sh ` (git skipped for speed; the fixture gets the CURRENT templates/hb-viz.js). trap-cleanup kills the server and rm -rf the temp dir on exit. Then: (1) start `node /hb-viz.js --serve --port 0` in the background, read the chosen port from its stdout, and poll GET /state with `curl --max-time 1` until ready (bounded loop, ~<=2s, no fixed long sleep); (2) LIVENESS — GET /state on the running server, assert the JSON fragment shows P0T1 WITHOUT the t-done class; then mark it done THROUGH the CLI (`node /hb.js start P0T1` && `node /hb.js done P0T1`); GET /state AGAIN on the SAME server process and assert the fragment now shows P0T1 with class t-done — proving the endpoint re-reads the data live, no regenerate/restart (this is the defining difference from the baked file); (3) SECURITY — GET /state with header `Origin: http://evil.example` returns a non-2xx (403) status (DNS-rebinding defence), reusing the same server; (4) NON-LOOPBACK REFUSAL — `node /hb-viz.js --serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port

` (no --allow-remote) exits non-zero AND prints a refusal AND binds nothing: a follow-up `curl --max-time 1 http://0.0.0.0:

/state` fails to connect (no listener leaked); (5) SNAPSHOT REGRESSION — run AFTER step 2 (so P0T1 is done): `node /hb-viz.js ` (no --serve) still writes a self-contained dag-view.html asserting the VERBATIM T14 conditions — it contains BOTH `t-done` AND `P0T1`, and contains NO external `https?://` URL. Print VIZ-SERVE-OK on stdout only after all five pass. Budget: ~one bootstrap (no git) + one background server + ~4 short node CLI/gen spawns + bounded curls — comfortably under the 5s per-criterion gate timeout.

tasks.title: Implement --serve in plugin/templates/hb-viz.js
tasks.description: Refactor hb-viz.js to extract a single renderer renderBody(dag,state) -> { body, doneT, totalT, pct } holding the current status logic (done/active/pending/locked, gate passed/waiting, requires chips, progress). Snapshot mode (default, no --serve) wraps renderBody in the SAME full page as today so its output stays byte-compatible (T14: self-contained, contains t-done and P0T1, no external URL). Add flags parsed from argv: --serve, --port (default 8787; --port 0 = ephemeral, print the chosen port), --host (default 127.0.0.1), --allow-remote. In --serve mode start a node `http` server: refuse to bind a non-loopback host unless --allow-remote (write a refusal to stderr and exit non-zero — mirror py mcp_server _is_loopback_host: 127.0.0.1 / ::1 / localhost are loopback, and a hostname that is not an IP is NOT loopback). Validate the Origin header on every request (reject with 403 when an Origin is present and its hostname is not loopback — the DNS-rebinding defence, mirroring py _origin_ok). tasks.description: Add node-suite group T86 to tests/run-tests.sh (after T85) running docs/howto/gate-examples/viz-serve.sh and asserting its VIZ-SERVE-OK marker (guard on `command -v node`). Document the new capability: in plugin/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md extend the `/heartbeat viz` section to show `node <project-dir>/.hb/hb-viz.js <project-dir>/.hb --serve [--port N]` and explain snapshot-vs-live (live reads the data directly, always current, loopback-only); in README.md extend the viz line to mention `--serve` for a live view. GATE_VS.desc: hb viz --serve is a real, live, loopback-only dashboard: GET /state re-reads dag.json+state.json fresh (a CLI state change is reflected without restarting the server), a non-loopback Origin is refused (403), a non-loopback bind is refused without --allow-remote, snapshot mode is unchanged, and the proof is wired into the suite and the docs.

review.prompt: Refute that VS is done. Does viz-serve.sh actually start a RUNNING http server and hit it over the network — not just read a generated file? Does it prove LIVENESS specifically: state changed THROUGH the CLI is reflected by a second GET on the SAME server process (no regenerate, no restart)? Could VIZ-SERVE-OK print if any sub-check (liveness / Origin-403 / non-loopback-refusal / snapshot-regression) was silently skipped or errored (set -e? explicit exits?) — i.e. is it vacuous? Is the Origin check a genuine non-2xx, and the non-loopback refusal a genuine non-zero exit that binds nothing? Is snapshot mode truly byte-compatible (T14 still green: self-contained, t-done + P0T1 present, no external URL) or did the refactor break it? Does the proof FAIL on the pre-implementation code (no --serve), reproducing the need, rather than passing vacuously? Is the server loopback-only by default, so this doesn't open an unauthenticated port to the network?

criteria.desc: the serve proof passes end-to-end (live re-read of a CLI state change + Origin-403 + non-loopback refusal binds nothing + snapshot regression asserts the verbatim T14 conditions: t-done AND P0T1, no external URL)
the proof is wired into the node suite (runs it + asserts its marker) so it re-verifies as a regression
the --serve capability is documented in the skill and the README
